Ezekiel's catalogue of Tyre's trade runs through metals, beasts and the "persons of men" (Ezek 27:13), and Joel and Amos condemn the nations who sold Judah's children and delivered whole captivities (Joel 3:3, 6; Amos 1:6, 9). Revelation's cargo is a twenty-eight-item inventory with a downward trajectory: it begins with sacred things and ends with "slaves, and souls of men." A system that sells what Yahuah made holy will at last sell people.

symbols.gloss: Babylon sunk beyond any rising
symbols.corner: At the Red Sea Pharaoh's host "sank into the bottom as a stone" and "sank as lead in the mighty waters" (Exod 15:5, 10), remembered in Nehemiah as "a stone into the mighty waters" (Neh 9:11). Jeremiah gives Seraiah his scroll against Babylon with a command: bind a stone to it and cast it into Euphrates, and say, "Thus shall Babylon sink, and shall not rise" (Jer 51:63-64). The mighty angel of Revelation 18:21 performs Jeremiah's sign-act on the cosmic scale, a great millstone hurled into the sea: Babylon sinks and never rises. The judgment is a single act and final, not a long future campaign.

symbols.gloss: the life of a system ended
symbols.corner: Jeremiah pronounces the sentence on Judah three times, then turns it on the nations: "I will take from them the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle" (Jer 25:10). Isaiah adds, "the mirth of tabrets ceaseth" (Isa 24:8), and over Tyre Yahuah says, "the sound of thy harps shall be no more heard" (Ezek 26:13). Revelation 18:22-23 repeats the inventory almost word for word: music, craft, millstone, lamp and wedding all fall silent. The silence is the verdict itself. It is a system that no longer exists.

symbols.gloss: undetectable manipulation of perception and will
symbols.corner: Torah forbids every enchanter, witch and charmer as an abomination (Deut 18:10-12), and Jehu names Jezebel's "whoredoms" and "witchcrafts" together (2 Kgs 9:22). Isaiah tells Babylon that loss and widowhood will come "for the multitude of thy sorceries" (Isa 47:9), and Nineveh is "the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms" (Nah 3:4). Revelation's pharmakeia is the manipulation of people's perception and will through means they could not detect or resist. The deception was so complete that the deceived could only mourn, not repent. Sorcery and harlotry stand together in every text, because both trade covenant loyalty for a power that is not Yahuah's.

symbols.gloss: the redeemed people as Yahuah's dwelling
symbols.corner: Yahuah remembers Israel's youth, "the love of thine espousals" (Jer 2:2), and swears covenant over her at Ezek 16:8. "Thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah of hosts is his name" (Isa 54:5), and the city is rebuilt with sapphires and carbuncles; "as the bridegroom rejoiceth over the bride, so shall thy Elohim rejoice over thee" (Isa 62:5). Ezekiel closes with the city's name, Yahuah shammah (Ezek 48:35). In Revelation the city and the Bride are the same thing, not primarily a place but a people. She is accepted and then dressed, and the order matters; she descends already prepared because everything was finished at the cross.

symbols.gloss: enemies' blood from the winepress
symbols.corner: Judah's blessing foretells one who "washed his garments in wine, and his clothes in the blood of grapes" (Gen 49:11). Isaiah sees him come from Edom "with dyed garments from Bozrah": "I have trodden the winepress alone... and their blood shall be sprinkled upon my garments" (Isa 63:1-3). The robe of Revelation 19:13 is therefore not His own blood from the cross but Isaiah's winepress blood of enemies. He is dipped in blood before the battle even starts, because the outcome was settled before the armies gathered. The blood of the tree opened the way; this blood is the sentence on those who refused it.

symbols.gloss: the redeemed following, Messiah alone judging
symbols.corner: At Sinai Yahuah "came with ten thousands of saints" (Deut 33:2); Joel hears Yahuah utter His voice before His army (Joel 2:11); Zechariah closes, "Yahuah my Elohim shall come, and all the saints with thee" (Zech 14:5). The armies following on white horses wear the bride's fine linen, "clean and white" (Rev 19:8, 14), so the book reads them as the redeemed. They carry no weapons and do not fight; Messiah alone executes judgment with the sword of His mouth. "Which were in heaven" says where the followers come from, not that they ruled there. The picture of saints returning from a heavenly reign is foreign to the text: one return, one judgment, and no earthly kingdom to follow.

symbols.symbol: Great Supper of Yahuah (Feast of the Birds)
symbols.gloss: the wicked's supper beside the marriage supper
symbols.corner: Torah's curse leaves the disobedient as "meat unto all fowls of the air" (Deut 28:26), and David promises Goliath's host to the birds (1 Sam 17:46). Zephaniah announces, "Yahuah hath prepared a sacrifice, he hath bid his guests" (Zeph 1:7), and after Gog Ezekiel summons every feathered fowl "to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you" (Ezek 39:17). Revelation's great supper is that sacrificial feast with Yahuah as host, the marriage supper seen from the side of evil. Two suppers stand at the end of the book, one for the bride and one for the birds; there is no third table. Every guest is seated at one or the other.

symbols.symbol: Lake of Fire and the Second Death
symbols.gloss: final sentencing and permanent removal
symbols.corner: "The wicked shall perish... into smoke shall they consume away" (Ps 37:20); Malachi says they "shall be ashes under the soles of your feet" (Mal 4:3), and Daniel's beast is "slain, and his body destroyed, and given to the burning flame" (Dan 7:11). The lake of fire is a sentencing, permanent removal rather than evil preserved forever: "the wages of sin is death" (Rom 6:23). The "for ever and ever" of Rev 14:11 and 20:10 speaks as Isaiah does of Edom, whose smoke "shall go up for ever" (Isa 34:10), and as Jude of Sodom, "suffering the vengeance of eternal fire" (Jude 7): a sentence final and never reversed, though the fire no longer burns.

symbols.symbol: Key of the Abyss and the Great Chain
symbols.gloss: Satan's authority stripped at the cross
symbols.corner: "Shall the prey be taken from the mighty, or the lawful captive delivered? ... Even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away" (Isa 49:24-25). Isaiah sees the host of the high ones "gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the pit, and shall be shut up in the prison" (Isa 24:22), and the key of David laid on a shoulder, "he shall open, and none shall shut" (Isa 22:22). In Revelation 20 Yahuah holds the lock, not the enemy. Satan was bound at the cross as the strong man (Matt 12:29; Col 2:15): authority stripped, not enemy eliminated. The thousand years is the present age of the gospel, not a future earthly kingdom.

symbols.gloss: new life in Messiah through the age
symbols.corner: Hosea promises, "after two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up" (Hos 6:2), and Isaiah, "Thy dead men shall live" (Isa 26:19). Ezekiel stands in the valley of dry bones and is told to prophesy until breath enters them: "I shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live" (Ezek 37:14). The first resurrection of Revelation 20 is spiritual and present, pictured by those bones: a person coming to life in Messiah throughout the gospel age. The bodily resurrection of Daniel 12:2 comes once, at the return. The futurist scheme of a pre-tribulation resurrection, then a millennium, then another resurrection, multiplies what the text keeps single.

symbols.gloss: total opposition named, not mapped
symbols.corner: Magog first appears among the sons of Japheth (Gen 10:2). Ezekiel gathers Gog "of the land of Magog" with Persia, Ethiopia, Libya, Gomer and Togarmah out of the north parts, against a people dwelling safely, and Yahuah answers with "an overflowing rain, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone" (Ezek 38:22). In Revelation Gog and Magog are total opposition named, not a nation on a map: Ezekiel's worldwide coalition, the same war as chapters 16 and 19, now with the beast and false prophet already cast out (Rev 19:20). Charts that assign Gog to a modern state miss that Revelation spreads it over "the four quarters of the earth" (Rev 20:8).

symbols.gloss: the true assembly defined by governing authority
symbols.corner: Israel's camp was ordered tribe by tribe around the tabernacle (Num 2), and "Yahuah thy Elohim walketh in the midst of thy camp... therefore shall thy camp be holy" (Deut 23:14). Fire from heaven answers the soldiers sent against Elijah (2 Kgs 1:10-12) and rains on Gog with brimstone (Ezek 38:22), "and I will send a fire on Magog" (Ezek 39:6). The camp of the saints and the beloved city is the true assembly, defined by whose authority governs it, not by coordinates on a map; "Yahuah loveth the gates of Zion" (Ps 87:2). The fire falls in the confrontation that is not a battle: one weapon, one fire, one judgment. No earthly Jerusalem siege is required.

symbols.gloss: the just Judge ending the old order
symbols.corner: "Yahuah shall endure for ever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment" (Ps 9:7), and "righteousness and judgment are the habitation of his throne" (Ps 97:2). Daniel sees the Ancient of days seated, "whose garment was white as snow... his throne was like the fiery flame" (Dan 7:9). The earth waxes old like a garment (Isa 51:6). The great white throne is the final seat of a perfectly just Judge and the boundary between the old world and the new; earth and sky flee in the dissolution of the present order. One throne and one Judge: Yahuah judges, and the Son acts as the One He appointed (Acts 17:31), never as a second co-equal occupant.

symbols.gloss: Yahuah's record establishing each case
symbols.corner: Moses asks to be blotted "out of thy book which thou hast written," and Yahuah answers, "Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out" (Exod 32:32-33). David's tears are "in thy book" (Ps 56:8), and Yahuah renders "to every man according to his work" (Ps 62:12). Before the Ancient of days "the judgment was set, and the books were opened" (Dan 7:10), and a book of remembrance is written for those who fear Him (Mal 3:16). Yahuah has always kept the record, and the deeds establish the case. Works do not purchase entry, which comes by the blood; they testify, showing whose people were whose, and the reward follows what the works reveal.

symbols.gloss: creation replaced, not repaired
symbols.corner: The Psalmist sets the old order against the Creator: "They shall perish, but thou shalt endure... as a vesture shalt thou change them" (Ps 102:26). Isaiah announces, "behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered" (Isa 65:17), and promises that "from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me" there (Isa 66:22-23). Revelation 21:1 is not repair but replacement, something that belongs to a different order altogether. This is the consummation Sabbath, the fourth and final rest. The claim that the Sabbath ended at the cross collapses four Sabbaths into one; Isaiah keeps it into the new creation itself.

symbols.gloss: Yahuah's uncreated, never-dimming light
symbols.corner: "In thy light shall we see light" (Ps 36:9). Isaiah promises, "The sun shall be no more thy light by day... but Yahuah shall be unto thee an everlasting light" (Isa 60:19), and Zechariah sees a day where "at evening time it shall be light" (Zech 14:7). The city needs no sun, moon or night: its light is uncreated, direct and never dimming. "The glory of Elohim did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof" (Rev 21:23), where the Greek behind the KJV's "light" is luchnos, lamp: Yahuah is the light, the Son the lamp that bears it. The nations walk in it and bring willing worship, not tribute paid under duress.

symbols.gloss: the open book and closing door
symbols.corner: Eden's gate is shut and guarded after the fall (Gen 3:24). Isaiah binds up the testimony and seals the law among his disciples (Isa 8:16), and Daniel is told, "shut up the words, and seal the book, even to the time of the end" (Dan 12:4), with the word that "the wicked shall do wickedly" and only the wise shall understand (Dan 12:10). Revelation reverses the command: "Seal not the sayings of the prophecy of this book: for the time is at hand." While the book is in the reader's hands, the gate is open. "He that is unjust, let him be unjust still" marks the moment the time for change has permanently ended.
